intro: Today we work on three small things that make your English much clearer: the -s at the end of words (works, plays, watches), short forms like I'm, isn't and don't, and the melody of questions. Listen, copy and say everything out loud!
teachingNotes: Indonesian words don't change, and final consonant clusters are rare, so learners drop the -s (*'She work in a bank'). Stress that the -s is a real sound people listen for: it tells them 'he/she/it' or 'more than one'. Commonest errors: works said as 'work', and watches said as one syllable 'watch-s' instead of WATCH-iz.

Three ways to say -s, decided by the LAST SOUND of the base word, not the spelling: /s/ after p, t, k, f (works, stops, eats); /z/ after vowels and voiced sounds like b, d, g, l, m, n, v (plays, goes, lives, reads); /ɪz/, an extra syllable, after s, z, sh, ch, x and j/ge sounds (watches, washes, fixes, buses, dances, changes). goes and does are spelled -es but have NO extra syllable. Use the throat test (hand on the throat: buzz or no buzz). Accept a slightly weak /z/; the priority is (1) say the -s at all, (2) add the extra syllable where it belongs, and never add one where it doesn't ('work-es', 'like-es').

Contractions: I'm is one syllable (it rhymes with 'time'); isn't = IZ-nt and doesn't = DUZ-nt (the s sounds like z); don't has the o of 'go', not the o of 'on'. The n't carries the 'no', so the n must be heard even when the final t is very light. Short yes answers are never contracted: 'Yes, I am', not 'Yes, I'm'. Only contractions of be and do/does are expected here.

Intonation, as a simple rule for A1: yes/no questions (Are…? Is…? Do…? Does…?) go UP at the end; wh- questions (What, Where, When, Who, How…) go DOWN at the end. Indonesian speakers often rise on every question (Indonesian 'Kamu tinggal di mana?' often rises), so 'Where do you live?' with a rise is the typical error. Don't teach exceptions (friendly rising wh- questions, tag questions).

Use only grammar the learner knows: be, simple present routines, short questions. No past simple (except was/were), no future, no perfect. Phonetic symbols: only /s/, /z/ and /ɪz/; describe everything else in simple words and with the arrows ↗ ↘.

keyPoints.title: Three sounds for -s
keyPoints.explanation: Never drop the -s. Listen to the last sound of the base word (not the last letter): after p, t, k, f the -s is /s/, a soft s (works); after a vowel sound or a 'buzzing' sound it is /z/, like the z of zebra (plays, lives); after s, z, sh, ch, x or a j sound it is /ɪz/, said 'iz', an extra syllable (watches = WATCH-iz). goes is spelled -es but stays one syllable.

examples.id: Rina main bulu tangkis setiap hari Minggu. (plays: /z/)

examples.en: My father watches the news every evening.
examples.id: Ayahku menonton berita setiap malam. (watches: WATCH-iz)

keyPoints.title: Short forms (contractions)
keyPoints.explanation: In speech we join words: I am → I'm, is not → isn't, do not → don't, does not → doesn't. I'm is one syllable. Say the n of n't clearly: it is the 'no' in the sentence.

examples.en: The office isn't open on Sundays.

keyPoints.title: Questions: up or down?
keyPoints.explanation: Yes/no questions go up at the end ↗ (Are you tired? Do you work here?). Wh- questions go down at the end ↘ (Where do you live? What's your name?).

assessment.rubric: Correct: closes (CLOSE-iz, after a z sound). 'goes' = 0: it is spelled -es but ends with /z/, one syllable. 'plays' = 0.

assessment.rubric: Correct: likes (after k, -s is /s/). 'reads' and 'calls' end with /z/ = 0.

blocks.text:
In Indonesian, words don't change: *dia bekerja*, *mereka bekerja*. In English, the **-s** at the end is a real sound that people listen for. It has two jobs:
- on a **verb** (a doing word) it means **he / she / it**: *she works*, *Budi plays*;
- on a **noun** (the name of a thing) it means **more than one**: *two books*, *three bags*.

So **never drop it**: *She work* sounds wrong. The -s has two quiet sounds. The symbols between slashes show sounds, not letters:
- **/s/** = a soft 's' like in *sapu*. After **p, t, k, f** (no buzz in your throat): *works, eats, stops, books*.
- **/z/** = the 'z' of *zebra*, with a buzz. After a **vowel sound** (a, e, i, o, u) or a buzzing sound like **b, d, g, l, m, n, v**: *plays, goes, lives, reads, bags*.

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata tidak berubah: *dia bekerja*, *mereka bekerja*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **-s** di akhir kata adalah bunyi nyata yang didengarkan orang. Tugasnya ada dua:
- di **kata kerja** artinya **he / she / it** (dia, satu orang atau benda): *she works*, *Budi plays*;
- di **kata benda** (nama benda) artinya **lebih dari satu**: *two books*, *three bags*.

Jadi **jangan pernah menghilangkannya**: *She work* terdengar salah. Akhiran -s punya dua bunyi pendek. Simbol di antara garis miring menunjukkan bunyi, bukan huruf:
- **/s/** = 's' pelan seperti di *sapu*. Sesudah **p, t, k, f** (leher tidak bergetar): *works, eats, stops, books*.
- **/z/** = 'z' seperti di *zebra*, bergetar. Sesudah **bunyi vokal** (a, e, i, o, u) atau bunyi yang bergetar seperti **b, d, g, l, m, n, v**: *plays, goes, lives, reads, bags*.

blocks.text: The throat test: put a hand on your throat and say *ssss*, then *zzzz*. /z/ buzzes, /s/ doesn't. If /z/ is hard, a soft /s/ is OK at first. The most important thing is to **say the -s**.

id.text: Tes leher: letakkan tangan di leher lalu ucapkan *ssss*, kemudian *zzzz*. /z/ bergetar, /s/ tidak. Kalau /z/ masih sulit, /s/ yang lembut boleh dulu. Yang paling penting adalah **mengucapkan -s-nya**.

blocks.prompt: Which verb ends with the sound /z/ (with a buzz)?
blocks.explain: play ends with a vowel sound, so the -s buzzes: /z/. work and eat end with k and t, so the -s is /s/.

id.explain: play berakhir dengan bunyi vokal, jadi -s-nya bergetar: /z/. work dan eat berakhir dengan k dan t, jadi -s-nya /s/.

blocks.text: A **syllable** is one beat of a word: *ma-kan* has 2, *bus* has 1. After the sounds **s, z, sh, ch, x** and **j** (often spelled *ge*), the ending is said **'iz'** (written /ɪz/) and the word gets **one more syllable**: *watch* → **WATCH-iz**, *wash* → **WASH-iz**, *fix* → **FIX-iz**, *bus* → **BUS-iz**, *change* → **CHANGE-iz**. Why? Two hissing sounds together (*watch* + *s*) are almost impossible to say, so English puts a small 'i' between them. Saying *watches* as one syllable (*watch-s*) is a very common mistake. Look at the **last sound**, not the spelling: *goes* and *does* end in -es but have **no** extra syllable.

id.text: **Suku kata** = satu ketukan dalam kata: *ma-kan* punya 2, *bus* punya 1. Sesudah bunyi **s, z, sh, ch, x** dan **j** (sering ditulis *ge*), akhirannya dibaca **'iz'** (ditulis /ɪz/) dan katanya mendapat **satu suku kata tambahan**: *watch* → **WATCH-iz**, *wash* → **WASH-iz**, *fix* → **FIX-iz**, *bus* → **BUS-iz**, *change* → **CHANGE-iz**. Kenapa? Dua bunyi mendesis berturut-turut (*watch* + *s*) hampir tidak bisa diucapkan, jadi bahasa Inggris menyisipkan 'i' kecil di antaranya. Mengucapkan *watches* sebagai satu suku kata (*watch-s*) adalah kesalahan yang sangat umum. Perhatikan **bunyi terakhir**, bukan ejaannya: *goes* dan *does* berakhiran -es tapi **tidak** punya suku kata tambahan.

blocks.text: Don't add the extra syllable everywhere: *works* and *eats* stay one syllable. Only the 'hissing' sounds s, z, sh, ch, x and j get **-iz**.

id.text: Jangan tambahkan suku kata ekstra di semua kata: *works* dan *eats* tetap satu suku kata. Hanya bunyi 'mendesis' s, z, sh, ch, x dan j yang mendapat **-iz**.

blocks.explain: fix ends with x (/ks/), so -es adds a syllable: FIX-iz, two syllables.

id.explain: fix berakhir dengan x (/ks/), jadi -es menambah satu suku kata: FIX-iz, dua suku kata.

material.title: Why 'goes' has no extra syllable but 'dances' does

blocks.text:
In Indonesian, what you write is almost always what you say. In English it **isn't**: the last **letter** and the last **sound** are often different. A final **e** is often silent, and **ce**, **ge** or **x** stand for other sounds. So the -s rule **doesn't look at the last letter**. It listens to the **last sound you say**.

So don't look, **say it**: say the plain word out loud (without -s) and listen to how it ends.
- It ends with **s, z, sh, ch, x** or **j** → add a beat: **'iz'**.
- Anything else → no new beat, just **/s/** or **/z/**.

id.text:
Dalam bahasa Indonesia, yang ditulis hampir selalu sama dengan yang diucapkan. Dalam bahasa Inggris **tidak begitu**: **huruf** terakhir dan **bunyi** terakhir sering berbeda. Huruf **e** di akhir sering tidak dibaca, dan **ce**, **ge** atau **x** mewakili bunyi lain. Karena itu aturan -s **tidak melihat huruf terakhir**, tapi **mendengar bunyi terakhir yang diucapkan**.

Jadi jangan dilihat, tapi **ucapkan**: ucapkan kata dasarnya (tanpa -s) dengan keras, lalu dengarkan bunyi akhirnya.
- Berakhir bunyi **s, z, sh, ch, x** atau **j** → tambah satu ketukan: **'iz'**.
- Bunyi lainnya → tidak ada ketukan baru, cukup **/s/** atau **/z/**.

rows.id: go berakhir bunyi 'o' (vokal) → goes = 1 ketukan, -s dibaca z
dibaca 'DUZ' → 1 ketukan; bunyi o-nya juga berubah, hafalkan saja
e tidak dibaca, bunyi terakhir 'v' → lives = 1 ketukan, dibaca 'LIVZ'
ce dibaca 's' → bunyi s → DANCE-iz = 2 ketukan
ge dibaca 'j' → bunyi j → CHANGE-iz = 2 ketukan
x dibaca 'ks' → bunyi s di akhir → FIX-iz = 2 ketukan

blocks.text: Two tricks to remember. If the word **already ends in a hissing sound** (s, sh, ch, x, ce, ge), you'll hear the extra 'iz'. And **-es after o** (*goes, does*) is only spelling: no extra beat. When you're not sure, say the plain word out loud: trust your ears, not your eyes.

id.text: Dua trik supaya gampang ingat. Kalau katanya **sudah berakhir bunyi mendesis** (s, sh, ch, x, ce, ge), kamu akan mendengar tambahan 'iz'. Dan **-es sesudah o** (*goes, does*) hanya soal ejaan: tidak ada ketukan tambahan. Kalau ragu, ucapkan kata dasarnya dengan keras: percayai telingamu, bukan matamu.

blocks.prompt: Which word gets an extra syllable (an extra 'iz')?
blocks.explain: wash ends with a 'sh' sound, a hissing sound, so washes is WASH-iz, two beats. live ends with a 'v' sound (the e is silent) and work with a 'k' sound, so lives and works stay one beat.

id.explain: wash berakhir bunyi 'sh', bunyi mendesis, jadi washes dibaca WASH-iz, dua ketukan. live berakhir bunyi 'v' (e-nya tidak dibaca) dan work berakhir bunyi 'k', jadi lives dan works tetap satu ketukan.

id.title: Kenapa 'goes' tidak punya suku kata tambahan tapi 'dances' punya?

blocks.text:
In conversation we join small words. These short forms are called **contractions**. The **'** (apostrophe) shows where letters are missing: **I am → I'm**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**, **do not → don't**, **does not → doesn't**.

How to say them:
- **I'm** is one beat, said like 'aim' (it rhymes with *time*).
- **isn't** sounds like **IZ-nt** and **doesn't** like **DUZ-nt**: the s sounds like z.
- **don't** is said 'dount', with the *o* of *go*, not the *o* of *on*.

The **n't** means 'not', so say the **n** clearly, or people may hear the opposite.

id.text:
Dalam percakapan kita menggabungkan kata-kata kecil. Bentuk singkat ini disebut **kontraksi** (contractions). Tanda **'** (apostrof) menunjukkan tempat huruf yang hilang: **I am → I'm**, **is not → isn't**, **are not → aren't**, **do not → don't**, **does not → doesn't**.

Cara mengucapkannya:
- **I'm** satu ketukan, dibaca 'aim' (berima dengan *time*).
- **isn't** terdengar seperti **IZ-nt** dan **doesn't** seperti **DUZ-nt**: huruf s-nya berbunyi z.
- **don't** dibaca 'dount', seperti *o* di *go*, bukan *o* di *on*.

**n't** berarti 'tidak', jadi ucapkan **n**-nya dengan jelas, kalau tidak orang bisa mendengar kebalikannya.

blocks.text: Short **yes** answers don't use short forms: *Yes, I am.* / *Yes, she is.*, not *Yes, I'm.* Why? A short form is weak and can't be the **last** word you say; the last word needs its full, strong sound. Short **no** answers can use them, because *not* or *n't* comes last: *No, I'm not.* / *No, she isn't.*

id.text: Jawaban singkat **yes** tidak memakai bentuk singkat: *Yes, I am.* / *Yes, she is.*, bukan *Yes, I'm.* Kenapa? Bentuk singkat itu lemah dan tidak bisa jadi kata **terakhir** yang diucapkan; kata terakhir perlu bunyi penuh yang kuat. Jawaban singkat **no** boleh memakainya, karena *not* atau *n't* ada di akhir: *No, I'm not.* / *No, she isn't.*

blocks.prompt: Why must you say the n in don't and isn't clearly?
options: It makes the sentence a question.
It shows more than one person.
blocks.explain: n't = not. Without it, 'I don't like it' sounds like 'I like it'.

id.explain: n't = not (tidak). Tanpa itu, 'I don't like it' terdengar seperti 'I like it'.

blocks.text:
**Intonation** is the melody of your voice: going up or down. The melody at the end of a question tells people what kind of question it is.
- **Yes/no questions** start with *Are, Is, Do, Does…* and **go up at the end ↗**: *Are you hungry? Do you work here?*
- **Wh- questions** start with a question word: *What, Where, When, Who, Why*, and also **How**. *How* has no w-h at the start, but it belongs to the same group. They **go down at the end ↘**: *What's your name? Where do you live?*

Many Indonesian speakers go up at the end of every question, because Indonesian questions often rise. In English, a wh- question that goes up can sound surprised or unsure.

id.text:
**Intonasi** adalah nada suara: naik atau turun. Nada di akhir pertanyaan memberi tahu orang jenis pertanyaannya.
- **Pertanyaan yes/no** diawali *Are, Is, Do, Does…* dan **naik di akhir ↗**: *Are you hungry? Do you work here?*
- **Pertanyaan wh-** diawali kata tanya: *What, Where, When, Who, Why*, dan juga **How**. *How* tidak diawali w-h, tapi masuk kelompok yang sama. Nadanya **turun di akhir ↘**: *What's your name? Where do you live?*

Banyak penutur Indonesia menaikkan nada di akhir setiap pertanyaan, karena pertanyaan bahasa Indonesia sering naik. Dalam bahasa Inggris, pertanyaan wh- yang naik bisa terdengar kaget atau ragu.

blocks.text: A quick test: can you answer with **yes** or **no**? Then go **up** ↗. Do you need information (a name, a place, a time)? Then go **down** ↘.

id.text: Tes cepat: bisakah dijawab dengan **yes** atau **no**? Kalau bisa, nadanya **naik** ↗. Butuh informasi (nama, tempat, waktu)? Kalau begitu, nadanya **turun** ↘.

blocks.prompt: Which question usually goes UP at the end?
blocks.explain: Are you hungry? is a yes/no question, so it goes up. The other two start with wh- words, so they go down.

id.explain: Are you hungry? adalah pertanyaan yes/no, jadi nadanya naik. Dua lainnya diawali kata wh-, jadi nadanya turun.

id.intro: Hari ini kita melatih tiga hal kecil yang membuat bahasa Inggrismu jauh lebih jelas: bunyi -s di akhir kata (works, plays, watches), bentuk singkat seperti I'm, isn't dan don't, serta nada pertanyaan. Dengarkan, tirukan, dan ucapkan semuanya dengan suara keras!
